title: Normalized module comparisons for a given nerve and its localized sites
statement: Let (C,J) and (E,K) be small sites, with E having finite limits and K subcanonical. Let F:E → Sh(J) be fully faithful and finite-limit preserving, and let N:Sh(J) ≃ Sh(K) have underlying presheaf functor naturally isomorphic to B ↦ Hom(F(-),B) [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-subcategory-comparison]. Let R and S be commutative ring sheaves and g:(Sh(K),S) → (Sh(J),R) a ringed equivalence with g.inverse=N.functor and invertible structural map. Fix a RingedPresentationAt g whole module transport [def-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-comparison-data]. For every X:E fix element-site slice adjunction data for F(X) [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] and an equivalence s_X:Sh(J)/F(X) ≃ Sh(K.over X) whose presheaf formula is Hom over F(X), restricted along Over.post F. For every f:X → Y fix the canonical element-map continuity proof. Then there are ringed equivalences from (K.over X,S.over X) to the element sites of (F(X),R), whose inverse images are the specified fibre equivalence followed by s_X, with invertible ring maps and module transports tied to their induced direct images. The whole-to-slice and further-restriction module functors have natural isomorphisms to the actual overFunctor and overMap of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. These can be chosen so that restriction through Y equals direct restriction to X with overFunctorMap, further restriction at an identity is identity, and further restrictions along f and h compose to that along f≫h, with the exact heterogeneous equations in RingedNerveSliceTransport. No site construction, binary cover, generators, subterminals, derived categories or adjoint mates are part of this conclusion.

proof.text: Apply the fibre description of localization to each chosen slice nerve. At (T → X), a map into the restricted ring is a map F(T) → |R| together with the fixed structure component F(T) → F(X). Projection to the R component identifies it with N(|R|)(T), and hence with S(T) using the invertible structural map of g. Its inverse pairs the R component with that fixed structure component. These maps preserve zero, one, addition and multiplication because each is computed on the R component. They are natural in T. This identifies the transported coefficient ring with S.over X, not merely an unrelated isomorphic coefficient ring.

proof.text: Conjugate each slice nerve by the specified element-site fibre equivalence. The preceding ring isomorphism and the slice geometric adjunction give its structural map; preservation of the four operations proves the RingData laws. This is the localized ringed-equivalence construction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-equivalence-slices], with the actual localized site as target. Construct the induced module direct image by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-induced-modules]. Apply the module-operation transport in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] to obtain RingedPresentationAt on the slice, retaining its underlying inverse-image comparison and its structural rank-one equation.

proof.text: On the canonical transported module operations, restriction sends a lift (m,c) to m, with inverse m ↦ (m,c). Addition and scalar action are computed on m, so both maps are linear. Naturality in the module follows from postcomposition, and naturality in (T → X) from precomposition. For an arrow f:X → Y the identical projection from the pullback over F(Y) gives the further-restriction isomorphism. The target functors are the actual overFunctor and overMap of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; their coefficient maps and overFunctorMap have identity section maps.

proof.text: Check the three equations on sections. The direct restriction comparison and its factorization through Y both return the original module component m. For the identity arrow the component is m ↦ m. For f:X → Y and h:Y → Z the direct comparison and the two successive comparisons again return m. Equality of the underlying natural transformations implies equality of module maps by faithfulness; rewriting the coefficient and functor composition identities supplies precisely the displayed heterogeneous equalities. Empty fibres, zero rings and empty covering sieves obey the same calculations; no choice of a lift is made.

proof.text: The chosen whole presentation has inverse isomorphic to the specified induced module direct image. Compare it to the transported-operation presentation by the unique adjunction-compatible left-adjoint isomorphism. Conjugate every whole-to-slice comparison by this single isomorphism; use the same choice at every slice. Naturality of this comparison proves that the inverse conjugating factors cancel in the restriction-composition equation. The further comparisons are unchanged. Thus all three equations persist for the specified whole presentation. This proves the claimed package without imposing subterminality or choosing any presenting site.

theorem exists_ringedNerveSliceTransport
    {C E : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory E] [HasFiniteLimits E]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} (K : GrothendieckTopology E) [K.Subcanonical]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u})
    (F : E ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u)) [F.Full] [F.Faithful] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (N : Sheaf J (Type u) ≌ Sheaf K (Type u))
    (n : N.functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf K (Type u) ≅ sheafSubcategoryNerve F)
    (g : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings S) (localCoefficientRings R))
    (inverseNerve : g.inverse = N.functor) [IsIso g.ringMap]
    (whole : RingedPresentationAt g)
    (sourceSlice : ∀ X : E, RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData
      (localCoefficientRings R) (F.obj X))
    (slice : ∀ X : E, Over (F.obj X) ≌ Sheaf (K.over X) (Type u))
    (sliceFormula : ∀ X : E,
      (slice X).functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (K.over X) (Type u) ≅
        yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft (Over X)ᵒᵖ
          (Over (F.obj X))ᵒᵖ (Type u)).obj (Over.post F).op)
    (continuous : ∀ {X Y : E} (f : X ⟶ Y),
      Functor.IsContinuous (elementMap (F.map f))
        (elementTopology (F.obj X)) (elementTopology (F.obj Y))) :
    Nonempty (RingedNerveSliceTransport R S g whole F sourceSlice slice continuous)
